pr.title: Keep a loop take running when the heartbeat falls behind its wraps (recording.md §15.4)
pr.head: 85b6da2e39a5fb04111992827ead723771ba6198

summary: A loop take is field record --loop: the daemon, field-audiod, loops a region of the song, [at, until), and records one take per pass. Two threads share the work. The audio callback runs every block on the audio thread, writes samples into the current take, and at each wrap, the sample where the region loops back to at, switches to the next pass's take. The heartbeat is a 250 ms timer on the message thread that finalizes each finished take, which writes its manifest and fires the take event, and opens the next pass's take ahead of the next wrap. That next take is the standby.

Issue #203 read two races from the code, both hit when the heartbeat falls behind the wraps, which the slow Windows CI runner did often. A wrap before the heartbeat serviced the last pass stopped the loop for good. A wrap while the heartbeat was finalizing found no standby, the callback took a late one over in the middle of a pass, and the heartbeat then lost track of which take was recording and dereferenced null at the next pass, crashing the daemon.

The fix makes the callback count what it did instead of leaving the heartbeat to guess. capturesEnded counts the takes the callback has ended, and takes end in the order the heartbeat opened them, so the heartbeat moves each ended take out and the next one up. The callback takes a standby over only at a wrap, so a pass that begins with none ready is skipped whole and counted in record.missed, and every take is a whole pass. The heartbeat opens the next standby before it finalizes. Stop discards a take still waiting for its wrap and finalizes a standby a wrap began just before it.

Since the first review, a session swap during a loop take carries the take's region onto the incoming session, as it carries the transport. Without the region, the clock ran past until and the new skip path landed a one-block take on every heartbeat tick, which field play --watch triggered by itself when the first take landed. The daemon now refuses a session the region does not fit, and the take goes on against the session already playing.

Two review rounds followed, and the head now answers both. The second found that a block ending exactly on until hid the wrap from the callback, so the take ran on through the next pass, a defect older than this pull request. The callback now ends a pass in the block that reaches until. A new test loops a region a whole number of blocks long. The review of this head found it clean, with one older suggestion left open: on a bed already rolling, the first take can begin a block after at.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Pass: one trip through the loop region, from at to until.
  • Wrap: the sample where a pass ends and the next begins, inside one audio block.
  • Heartbeat: the daemon's 250 ms timer on the message thread; Player::serviceCapture is its recording step.
  • Standby: the next pass's take, opened by the heartbeat and published to the callback through standbyCapture.
  • capture: the oldest loop take not yet handed to finalize, owned by the message thread.
  • Skipped pass: a pass that begins with no standby ready. It records nothing and adds one to record.missed.
  • Pending: what status reports for a take that exists but has not begun, now including a loop take waiting for its wrap.
  • Session swap: the session op replacing the playing live session with a fresh compile, which field play --watch sends after an edit.

cards.title: Review history
cards.html:

  • cb48e36: changes requested. A block ending exactly on until hid the wrap, so takes spanned two passes. Fixed in e37062f with here + n >= untilAt.
  • 85b6da2: clean. One-bar, two-bar, and 2.1–2.3 loops land one whole pass per take, a block-aligned punch-out keeps its length, the swap probes still pass, and punch-daemon.test.ts passed 10 of 10 in 14 runs. CI passed on windows and linux.
  • Not run. The MIDI daemon tests, which open every MIDI source, because a live field keys session runs on the review machine.

groups.title: How the callback and the heartbeat hand takes over
groups.kicker: A count of ended takes replaces the done flag, a standby starts only at a wrap, and a swap keeps the region
intro: The callback cannot allocate, lock, or touch files, so it never owns a take. It only reads two pointers the message thread publishes: activeCapture, the take it writes into, and standbyCapture, the take it switches to at the next wrap. The message thread owns the takes themselves in capture and standby, and the heartbeat has to work out after the fact what the callback did with them.

Before this change the heartbeat worked that out from a done flag and from whether standbyCapture was still set. Both went wrong once two wraps fell between ticks or a wrap fell inside a finalize. Now the callback adds one to capturesEnded for every take it ends, and the heartbeat moves that many takes out of capture, pulling standby up each time. Because takes begin and end in the order they were opened, the count alone says who owns what.
What a pass looks like when the heartbeat is late

1. The standby is ready at the wrap. The callback switches to it on the wrap sample and the passes meet on consecutive samples, as before. The wrap is the block that reaches until, including one that ends exactly on it, because the block after that one already starts at at.
  2. No standby is ready. The callback keeps running in a skipping state with no take, counts the pass in record.missed, and switches to the next standby only at a later wrap, never mid-pass.
  3. Stop arrives. Stop finalizes the take recording, finalizes a standby a wrap began just before it, discards a take still waiting for its wrap, and detaches twice, because the block in flight can take a standby over between the first detach and its own store.
A session swap keeps the take's region

The region a loop take records is set on the live session, and a session swap installs a new session object. carryTakeRegion sets the take's region on the incoming session twice: once before the pre-roll, so the chain warms inside the region, and again under the message thread's lock, which decides, because a take can start or stop in between. A session too short for the region is refused with an error, and the session already playing keeps the take. With a region carried, the swap locates the new session at the old one's unwrapped position, and the region wraps it to the same place.

checks.text: Every new callback step is an atomic load, store, exchange, or increment, so the audio thread still takes no lock and allocates nothing. The std::vector of ended takes lives in serviceCapture, on the message thread.

files.note: Replaces captureDone with capturesEnded, drops the finished slot, documents which take capture and standby hold under a loop, and declares carryTakeRegion and the serviceStallMs test seam.

checks.text: The counter is the whole protocol. The callback increments it once per ended take, and the heartbeat reads and zeroes it with one exchange, so an end that lands mid-service is counted on the next tick rather than lost.
Read once in the constructor from FIELD_AUDIOD_SERVICE_STALL_MS, and only with null output, so a real device never stalls.

files.note: The callback's skip state and wrap (recordAudioBlock), the heartbeat's count-driven handoff (serviceCapture), stop's handling of a waiting or just-begun standby (stopRecording), the region carry in loadSession, and pending in status.

checks.text: >= ends a pass in a block that ends exactly on until, which > missed because the next block already starts at at. Probed against a build of this head: [96000, 192000) landed four 96000-frame takes, [96000, 288000) two 192000-frame takes, and [96000, 144000) six 48000-frame takes. At cb48e36 they merged passes. A punch-out over exactly 48 blocks landed 24576 frames at both heads.
The only place a standby is taken over: at a wrap, whether or not the heartbeat has finalized the last pass. With none ready, the pass that begins here is counted and skipped.

A skipped pass ends no take, so it adds nothing to capturesEnded. Traced two and three wraps between ticks: the heartbeat moves out exactly the takes that ended and opens one standby per tick, so record.missed counts each skipped pass once.
A loop take waiting for its wrap has startedAt() < 0, so status reports it as pending. field record already keys its start line on pending, so a waiting take is not announced as begun.
Probed at this head: a session sent mid-loop kept loop_from and loop_to and landed seven whole passes, and field record --loop beside field play --watch landed no one-block take.

Probed: an edit that ended the song before the region made field play --watch print watch audiod session: a loop take is recording, and its region does not fit this session (stop first): …, and the take went on landing whole passes against the session already playing.
With a region carried, the old session's unwrapped position goes to the new one as it is, and the region wraps it. Clamping or wrapping it at the song's length would move the take's bed.

A swap during the take cached liveLoop as true, because the carried region makes the session loop. Converted delivery reads that flag to decide when the song ends, so stop recomputes it once the region clears.

Traced a stop racing a wrap: the block in flight can exchange standbyCapture before the first detach and store activeCapture after it. The exchange here catches that take, and the second two-epoch wait lets the block finish before finalize. No later block takes a standby over, because captureLoop is already false.
A take with no start is discarded only once a loop take has finalized. The loop's first take is capture until it finalizes, so a stop during a count-in still lands it, as a stop always did.
A standby with a start is the pass a wrap began just before the stop, so it lands as the stop's partial pass. The base discarded it with its samples.

Ran punch-daemon.test.ts at this head 10 times in a row and 4 at once, all 10 tests passing each time. The two race tests, which drive two wraps per tick and a wrap inside every finalize, fail at the base.

The next standby opens before any finalize, so a slow disk delays a take's manifest but costs no pass. When every take has ended, the new take goes straight into capture so status keeps reporting the loop.

groups.title: Tests that hold the heartbeat behind the wraps, swap mid-loop, and align the wrap with a block
groups.kicker: A region shorter than a tick, a stalled heartbeat, a swap during the take, and a region a whole number of blocks long
intro: Both races needed a heartbeat that falls behind, which a fast machine rarely produces. The tests force it two ways. A loop a tenth of a second long puts two or three wraps between 250 ms ticks. The stall seam holds the heartbeat 600 ms between moving a finished take out and finalizing it, longer than the 500 ms region, so a wrap lands inside every finalize.

Both tests poll status every 50 ms through followLoop and require each poll to report a recording loop with its take count, which is what the crash and the lost take broke. Both then require every landed pass to start at at and be exactly the region long, and every recording on disk to be complete.

A third test swaps the session mid-loop. A session whose bed ends before the region is refused with "does not fit", and the same song swapped in keeps the region and goes on landing whole passes. Passes near the swap may run a block long, because a block the callback misses while the swap holds the session's lock still records input, so the test holds only the passes clear of the swap to the region's exact length.
A fourth test loops a region exactly 48 blocks long. Blocks start on the grid the locate to at sets, so every pass ends exactly on a block boundary, the case the old wrap test missed.

files.note: Adds followLoop, the two race tests, the swap test, and the block-aligned region test, and clears FIELD_AUDIOD_SERVICE_STALL_MS after each test.

checks.text: The tests use a null device and their own temporary project and socket, and arm only audio input 1, so they open no real device and no MIDI source.
Against cd088df, the base handoff with only the seam added, this test failed in 3 of 3 runs with "timed out waiting for 4 passes to land".
missed > 0 holds by construction: the heartbeat opens at most one standby per tick, and two or more wraps fall between ticks.
Against cd088df this test failed in 3 of 3 runs with "field-audiod connection closed", the crash #203 describes.
The refusal leaves the take running against the session already playing, which the next swap then replaces.

A region exactly 48 null-clock blocks long, so every pass ends on a block boundary. Against the cb48e36 build this test failed with "timed out waiting for 3 passes to land", because no pass ever ended.

groups.title: What the docs, the plan, and the protocol say
groups.kicker: The skipped pass, the pending take, and the swap in audio-engine.md, an amendment to recording §15.4, and the status schema comment
intro: docs/audio-engine.md describes the daemon as it runs today. It now says the heartbeat finalizes every take that ended since its last tick, opens the next transaction first, skips a pass with none ready, reports a waiting take as pending, and carries the take's region across a session swap. The recording plan is completed, so it keeps its as-built record and gains a dated amendment under §15.4, the decision about loop takes, saying what the first build got wrong and what replaced it. The status schema's comment on pending names the loop case.

files.note: Comment only: pending also marks a loop's next take waiting for its wrap.
Rewrites the paragraph on missed passes in "Punch-out and loop takes" and adds one on session swaps.

checks.text: "Every take is a whole pass that starts at at" holds at this head, block-aligned regions included.
Matches the code and the probe: the swap keeps the region, and a session the region does not fit is refused while the take goes on.

files.note: Adds the 2026-10-11 amendment to §15.4, item 4, the loop-take decision.

checks.text: The amendment follows the plan's existing *Amended pattern instead of rewriting the as-built text, as docs/projects/README.md asks of a finished plan.
The amendment's last addition records the block-aligned wrap and the change to the test.
